Subject: Optera - dedicated capacity needs / request for proposal

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the product demo last week — team loved the latency profile. We're moving quickly on an internal evaluation and Procurement asked me to capture a few concrete dedicated capacity options we can review with finance. High level asks:

- Minimum guaranteed GPUs and baseline pricing for a 12-month commitment
- A suggested ramp schedule (month-by-month activation) so we can map spend to milestones
- Warm-start / pre-warm credits so we avoid cold KV cache impacts for our initial rollout
- Burst/overage behavior and SLAs for sustained spikes

We have an initial target workload: ~120 QPS of short-chat prompts (~1000 tokens avg) and a secondary embedding workload for nightly batch embeddings (~500k vectors/day). Preferred hardware: A100 / H100 class, but interested in Redwood's cost/latency options (quantized variants ok if quality is preserved).

Can you send a few concrete configs we can put into the procurement packet? Procurement would like to see a minimal footprint option and a recommendation for a 3-stage ramp plan tied to product milestones.

I've attached our short RFP summary. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Samir
VP Product, Optera Health

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear asks and the RFP, appreciate the detail. Below are three concrete reservation options with ramp and warm-start notes. I've attached a compact proposal PDF and an SLA/ramp sheet for procurement.

Quick summary (high-level):

1) Pilot lane (low-risk) — "Pilot-8"
- Minimum guaranteed: 8 x A100 80GB (shared pool, dedicated to Optera)
- Ramp cadence: immediate activation, aim for production traffic at month 2
- Use-case fit: feature validation / controlled rollout; supports ~35-45 QPS of chat traffic with burst capacity
- Warm-start: 200k token warm-start credit included to pre-populate key KV shards
- Price: monthly reserved fee + per-token overage; see attached PDF

2) Production baseline — "Baseline-32"
- Minimum guaranteed: 32 x A100 80GB (pinned lanes)
- Ramp cadence: month 0 -> 8, month 1 -> 16, month 2 -> 32 (full capacity)
- Use-case fit: steady 100-140 QPS chat + embeddings nightly load; targeted latency SLOs 95th < 250ms for standard generation models
- Warm-start: tiered credits + cache pre-warming window during onboarding
- SLA: 99.95%% uptime for dedicated lanes; detailed in SLA_Ramp_Timeline.xlsx

3) Growth + burst plan — "Floor+Burst"
- Baseline + burst pool: baseline 32 + shared burst pool (up to additional 24 GPUs across region)
- Auto-fallback: if pinned capacity suppressed, requests route to compatible quantized variants or cross-region lane with prioritized routing
- Financials: reserved discount tiers apply with 12-month commit; burst consumed at premium rate

Operational notes and tradeoffs:
- H100 migration path: optional 8->16 H100 subset for latency-sensitive models; we can provide a parallel lane for experiments
- KV caching: recommended pre-warm window of 48 hours when moving from pilot -> baseline to achieve steady-state latency
- Prefix caching: we can persist hot prefixes to reduce token compute in night windows for embeddings

Next steps I suggest:
- I'm happy to run this by our SE team to validate the throughput numbers against your prompt mix and embedding batch pattern.
- If procurement wants, we can provide a PO-ready quote and the SLA appendix for legal review.

When would you like a follow-up call? I have open slots Wed 11/4 and Thu 11/5 afternoon PST.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — thanks for the context. I ran a quick perf projection against Optera's numbers and attached an activation worksheet (SLA_Ramp_Timeline.xlsx) with nominal throughput curves. High level findings and recommended activation plan below.

Technical summary:
- Baseline-32 with A100-80GB (32 GPUs) should comfortably support steady 110-130 QPS of short-chat generation at ~1k tokens avg when we use continuous batching + prefix caching. Expected steady-state throughput: ~125 QPS (sampling gen, temp 0.7) with 95th-percentile latency ~210-240ms.
- Nightly embedding batch (500k vectors/day) can be handled in the baseline lane during off-peak hours if we schedule large batches across a 6-8 hour window; embedding throughput estimate ~85k vectors/hour on mixed-precision optimized kernels.
- Pilot-8 will support feature validation but we recommend not using it for their full nightly batch unless they shard embedding jobs to separate off-peak windows.

Warm-start / KV notes:
- Cold-run penalty observed in similar customers: 20-35%% tail latency hit until KV caches reach steady state. To mitigate we recommend:
  - 48 hours of warm-start window during onboarding (continuous dummy traffic + prefix preloading) — equivalent to ~300k tokens of warm-start credit.
  - Additionally, provide a 'burst pre-warm' of 100k tokens at each phase transition (8->16, 16->32) to accelerate cache fill.
- Expressed in contract: "Onboarding warm-start credit: 300,000 tokens; Phase-transition pre-warm credits: 100,000 tokens per activation step."

H100 migration guidance:
- For sub-50ms tail latency on the tightest models we recommend a small experimental H100 pool: 4 H100s as a proof-of-concept lane (can be expanded to 8 if traffice demands). H100s give ~1.6-2x single-token latency improvement vs A100 on attention-bound workloads.

Activation timeline (recommended):
- Week 0 (PO accepted): Provision Pilot-8; begin security onboarding + baseline metric collection (SLO targets and baseline prompts).
- Week 1-2: Pilot warm-start period (use onboarding credits); validate integration and run perf tests using customer's production prompt set in canary mode.
- Week 4: Activate 16 GPUs; run mixed traffic with staged cutover for 30%% of production traffic.
- Week 8: Full activation to 32 GPUs; run 48-72 hour stress window to validate steady-state latency.

Operational / billing notes:
- Billing: reserved monthly fee for pinned lanes + usage overage at per-token rates defined in Proposal_Dedicated_Offer_v3.pdf. Warm-start credits are consumed against token usage and are tracked in the Console.
- Burst behavior: shared-burst pool will be billed at premium overage rate; fallback routing to quantized variants occurs automatically when region saturation detected unless customer opts out.

Next steps and asks:
- Samir / Procurement: confirm desired start-of-PO week (target date by 11/24 for finance cutoffs).
- Grace: I'll attach the activation timeline + short technical appendix. Happy to jump on a technical call to walk through kernel selection and caching strategies; available Thu 11/12 PST.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
